pr_title: Implements Requires*Attribute on class behavior for NativeAOT
pr_body:
Implements most of the missing pieces to get Requires on class working correctly in NativeAOT.

Major changes:
* Detect Requires mismatch between derived and base class
* Warn on field access if the owning class has Requires
* Changes to reflection marking to warn on more cases (instance methods on Requires classes for example)

Supportive changes:
* The helpers to detect Requires attributes now return the found attribute view out parameter

Fixes #81158

Still two missing pieces - tracked by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/82447:
* Requires on attributes - NativeAOT doesn't handle this at all yet, part of it is Requires on the attribute class
* Avoid warning when DAM marking an override method which has Requires (or its class has) - this avoids lot of noise, NativeAOT currently generates these warnings in full

review_comments: Something I missed in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/83085: why did we decide to detect reflection access to RAF and RDC? I understand that nativeaot is able to do this, but I'm not sure it should. I liked @MichalStrehovsky's way of phrasing the question in https://github.com/dotnet/linker/issues/2739#issuecomment-1097551680, and based on that I would have said we shouldn't do this.

The reasoning is right below Michal's comment: https://github.com/dotnet/linker/issues/2739#issuecomment-1098026715

My main reason is: the compiler should be effectively bullet-proof, it either warns, or the thing works as before. Now we're never going to be there 100%, but we try (with only a few exceptions where we decided it's not worth the trouble). In this case, it's really easy to implement this in the compiler. We have to accept all of the related complexity because we need to support RUC, and thus supporting RDC/RAF is basically for free.

I guess to me RDC/RAF is a separate concern and it seems inconsistent to support those if the analyzers don't detect reflection access, or if AOT doesn't warn on SupportedOSPlatform reflection access. But I'm coming around to your point that it doesn't hurt, and might catch some issues that would have gone undetected otherwise. Thanks!
Nice! I look forward to ILLink matching this behavior too.

ILLink already does this: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/aeed019532e9e48b09f4ebc77bc862dc70dc0c0a/src/tools/illink/src/linker/Linker.Steps/MarkStep.cs#L3095-L3099

There are probably some holes around attributes (as per the referenced bug), but the main part already works (I ran into that in the tests).
I'm not sure I understand this - why do we need dataflow analysis for the type/base mismatch? Is it just an implementation detail (to avoid a new dependency node type maybe)?

You guessed it - there's no point in introducing another dependency node - so reusing the one we have already. Previously it only did generic parameter data flow, now it does RUC/RDC/RAF validation as well. I know it's not exactly "dataflow", but we're already using that term for basically everything analysis related in the compiler.
